newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Four Colombian rebels die in battle with army.
newsitem.headline: Four Colombian rebels die in battle with army.

text.p: Four leftist rebels died in a 10-hour firefight with the army in northwestern Colombia, military sources said on Friday.

The battle between counterinsurgency troops and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) began on Thursday in a rural zone near the town of Ituango, in trouble-torn Antioquia province. During the operation, soldiers discovered a rebel camp and seized mortar rounds, ammunition and anti-personnel mines.
Meanwhile, in southern Colombia, mothers of some of the 60 soldiers taken prisoner by FARC guerrillas more than two months ago launched their own efforts to free their sons.

Frustrated at the delay, a group of parents hoping to make contact with rebel commanders set sail on Thursday down a river in Caqueta province, near the zone earmarked for the eventual handover of the troops.

The soldiers were captured when the rebels overran a military base in Las Delicias in neighbouring Putumayo province on Aug. 30, killing at least 27 soldiers. The mothers' mission was sharply criticised by Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra who said the five-day river trip was "insensitive."

Negotiations to free the prisoners have been slow as the FARC insists that large swathes of southern Caqueta province be demilitarized and that an international mediation committee including foreign media be on hand to witness the handover.
The government is eager to avoid further humiliation and is loath to give the rebels a platform to project an international message.

In its latest communique sent late on Thursday, the FARC accused the army of increasing the troop presence in those areas earmarked for the handover. It added that regional FARC leaders holding the 60 soldiers would not meet mediators or representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross -- a meeting was expected to take place this week -- until troops were withdrawn from designated areas.
